s1.syndrome_frame: Purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and possible paraproteinemia
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
History of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease
Presented with altered mental status and unwitnessed fall
Purpuric lesions developed on nose, ear, and extensor surfaces of arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy findings showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein and elevated serum cryoglobulin levels

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and biopsy findings showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Plasma cell dyscrasia
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses and κ-light-chain restriction

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and lytic bony lesions, along with a bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, is highly suggestive of multiple myeloma. The presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: While Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia can present with similar laboratory abnormalities, the presence of lytic bony lesions and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells is more characteristic of multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and biopsy findings showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins, these findings can be seen in multiple myeloma, and the overall clinical picture is more consistent with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of amyloid deposits on biopsy, which is a hallmark of amyloidosis, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Plasma cell dyscrasia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes multiple myeloma, and the specific findings in this case are more consistent with multiple myeloma than a more general plasma cell dyscrasia.
